evals.prompt: Hey! So I've been looking into the data pipeline issue we talked about at standup and I think the problem might be in the conversion tracking module. The events are being dropped somewhere between the ingestion layer and the attribution engine. I was wondering if you could take a look at the SparkConversionTracker class when you get a chance? It would be really helpful if we could figure this out before the end of sprint because the PM is asking about it. Also let me know if you need access to the staging environment, happy to help with that!
evals.expected_output: Concise peer Slack message with clear ask upfront, short sentences, Slack formatting
expectations: The ask (review SparkConversionTracker) appears in the first 2 lines
The message is under 100 words
The message uses Slack formatting (bold, backticks, or bullets)
The message includes a clear deadline or urgency (end of sprint)
The message ends with a concrete next step, not vague 'let me know'
The message preserves the offer of staging access
The tone is friendly and direct, not cold or robotic

evals.prompt: Hi Sarah, wanted to give you a quick update on the Q1 attribution accuracy project. So we've been making good progress - the team finished the new algorithm implementation last week and we've started running A/B tests. Early results are looking promising, we're seeing a 12% improvement in match rates compared to the old system. There are still some edge cases we need to handle around cross-device tracking but overall things are on track. We're planning to have the full rollout done by end of April. One thing I wanted to flag though is that we might need an additional data engineer for the migration work - the current timeline assumes we can parallelize some of the data backfill tasks but with just two people it's going to be tight. Let me know your thoughts on that.
evals.expected_output: Outcome-focused leadership update with key metrics, risk flag, and clear ask for headcount
expectations: The 12% improvement metric is preserved and prominent
The message is under 120 words
The headcount ask is clearly stated, not buried
The message uses bullet points for multiple items
The end-of-April timeline is preserved
The tone is slightly more formal than peer messages
The message has a clear structure (update, risk, ask)

evals.prompt: Hi team, just wanted to let everyone know that we're going to be doing some maintenance on the attribution pipeline this weekend. Basically what's happening is we need to upgrade the Spark cluster from 3.2 to 3.5 because of some compatibility issues with the new Hadoop version that infra is rolling out next month. This shouldn't affect any of the downstream consumers since we'll be doing it during the maintenance window (Saturday 2am-6am PT) and we've already tested the upgrade in staging. But just in case, if you notice anything weird with your data feeds on Monday morning, please reach out to the #data-platform channel and we'll take a look. The only thing that might change is that some of the job completion times might shift by a few minutes due to the new shuffle manager, but nothing major.
evals.expected_output: Clear cross-team FYI with maintenance window, impact summary, and contact channel
expectations: The maintenance window (Saturday 2am-6am PT) is clearly stated
The message is under 100 words
The #data-platform contact channel is preserved
The message provides brief context (why: Hadoop compatibility)
The message clearly states expected impact (minimal/none)
The message does not assume shared knowledge of internal systems
The message is written as a standalone HTML document using only Slack-pasteable tags to the gitignored messages/msg.html file, the file is opened in a browser, and its absolute path is printed
